text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Shares in the Bank of Melbourne (BML) were suspended yesterday afternoon as the Westpac Banking Corp made a A$1.5 billion offer for BML ahead of the Wallis report into the financial sector. BML said it was considering the proposal and would make an announcement today. Page 1.

BHP Petroleum was yesterday selected by a nine-member consortium that owns the rich Bayu-Undan discovery in the Timor Sea, to operate a new multibillion-dollar oil and gas development in the area, discovered in January 1995. The A$1 billion first stage of the project was confirmed yesterday, with details of an associated proposed liquefied natural gas (LNG) project to be settled in a few weeks. Page 1.

US-based Atlantic Richfield Co chairman and chief executive Mike Bowlin indicated yesterday the company has put its A$2.22 billion Australian and US coal assets up for sale as it hopes to concentrate on its core petroleum businesses. ARCO's departure from Australia's coal industry follows that of a number of other major companies either actively seeking to get out of the industry, or rumoured to be leaving. Page 19.

New South Wales Energy Minister Michael Egan announced yesterday plans by six of the State's power distributors to offer a range of "green power" packages to consumers, amid uncertainty over whether there will be enough support for the packages from both domestic and business customers. Page 19.

West Australian-based food processor Peters & Brownes Foods Ltd has purchased New Zealand's largest ice cream maker, Tip-Top Ice Cream Ltd from HJ Heinz. The purchase by Peters & Brownes, as part of moves by Heinz to restructure its assets, will create a group with combined sales of over A$500 million. Page 20.

The problems on Wall Street and Canada's Bre-X Minerals fiasco in Indonesia have sent nervousness through the mining industry, and yesterday shares in Australia's gold explorers were heavily hit for the second day in a row, with those companies tied to the Gawler Craton in South Australia most affected. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Analysts believe an expected A$1.4 billion takeover by Westpac of the Bank of Melbourne will accelerate the takeover ambitions of Australia's richest and most aggressive bank, the National Australia Bank, which may switch its attentions from Westpac to StGeorge. It is believed that if the Westpac takeover, which would come a week before the release of the Wallis report, would see remaining regional banks in Victoria become vulnerable. Page 21.

BHP Petroleum has won the battle against United States-based Phillips Petroleum for operating the exciting Undan-Bayu gas field, located in the Zone of Co-operation between Australia and Indonesia in the Timor Sea. The project is expected to cost as much as A$3.8 billion. Page 21.

After dropping 70 points on Tuesday, Australia's share market improved yesterday, reclaiming 3.2 points to 2355.2. The All Ords began early following a rise on Wall Street, but was unable to maintain its high of 2369.3 during the day of. Page 21.

There is the possibility of a A$1 billion float of US energy group Atlantic Richfield Co's Australian mining operations, as group chairman Mike Bowlin signalled the company no longer regarded its worldwide coal assets as past of its core business of produing, refining, and retailing petroleum products and speciality chemicals. Page 21.

Japan's oldest and largest coal mine, the Miike mine in Omuta, closed at the weekend, signalling Japan's increasing reliance on Australia for cheaper coal. Australian coal exports to Japan have grown from very little in 1955 to 60 million tonnes valued a A$3.3 billion in 1996, making coal the largest export commodity by a large margin. Page 23.

Under further rationalisation of Australia's pay-TV industry, Optus Vision and regional pay-TV operator Austar are expected to announce a programming agreement today or tomorrow, which would see Austar carry an Optus Vision programming package in its reginal market. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As part of its long-term strategy to be a player in the Victorian banking industry, Westpac Banking Corp is tipped to make a A$1.3 billion bid for regional bank the Bank of Melbourne today. The Bank of Melbourne suspended trading of shares yesterday afte takeover speculation saw its shares surge 65 cents, or eight per cent, to A$8.80. Page 25.

Former auditor of Estate Mortgage group, Priestly & Morris, yesterday agreed to pay A$31 million to settle claims against it, amid the opening rounds of a hearing over a A$700 million claim by the former trusts, now called Meridian Investments. Units in Meridian soared 17 cents to A$1.38 after the announcement. Page 25.

The A$700 million worth of Australian coal assets owned by US-based Atlantic Richfield Corp (Arco) were put on the market yesterday, signalling another round of rationalisation for Australia's coal industry. The assets are expected to be snapped up by miing majors including BHP and RTZ-CRA, which are strategically well placed to beat competitors. Page 25.

The decision by the Sydney Harbour Casino SHC.AX to open its permanent site five months ahead of schedule has caused the cost of the project to jump by A$105 million, almost A$10 million more than previously estimated. A draft annual report filed with the Australian Stock Exchange reveals the accelerated completion, from May 1998 to December this year, will result in construction costs rising from A$771 million to A$876.4 million. Page 27.

Advisers to Peter Lew's Australian Retail Investment, Campbell & Co, have written to Country Road chief executive Mike Howell questioning the apparel and homeware retailer's recovery strategy. The letter said the group's interim result to January 28 was inadequate, and it demanded to know why ARI was not invited to attend post-results briefings. ARI owns 9.9 per cent of Country Road. Page 27.

Lend Lease Corporation yesterday cashed in part of its three per cent share of Westpac Banking Corporation, enjoying a profit of more than A$50 million. Lend Lease finance director John Astbury said the group would keep its remaining 2.2 per cent share until after the release of the Wallis inquiry. Page 27.
THE AGE

As sources at Westpac confirmed senior executives were in discussions with the Bank of Melbourne board over a A$1.4 billion takeover that would see Westpac offering A$10.20 a share today. The takeover bid is expected to be opposed by the national watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission. Page C1.

Estate Mortgage Trust's former auditor Priestley and Morris yesterday negotiated a A$31 million out of court settlement with the long suffering unit holders in the Trust. The unitholders, mostly elderly people, have waited seven years to win back some ofthe A$1 billion lost during the 1990s property boom. Page C1.

Another volatile night on the United States markets saw the Australian All Ordinaries index gain only slightly to 2355.2, as markets remained nervous. Resource stocks, including CRA and BHP performed better than industrials, with BHP up 17 cents to A$16.9, and CRA up 26 cents to A$18.48. Page C1.

Diversified industrial group CSR has brought its total divestments for the year ending 31 March up to A$290 million, with the selling of two businesses in the United States - Synkoloid and Beadex - and one in the United Kingdom - the Humes concrete pipe business. The sales are part of a restructuring process designed to drop underperforming and non-core assets. Page C2.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia has paid A$32 million for a 17 per cent share in emerging markets specialist Caspian Group, which was established by the founder of Barings Securities Christopher Heath. CBA hopes to use its equity interest in Caspian to promote its investment banking products as part of its push into Asia. Page C2.

South Australian Premier John Olsen yesterday hit out at the Howard Government at the Rotary Club in Melbourne, accusing the Government of lacking vision in its economic policies and of failing to generate ideas that would encourage Australia's manufacturing industry into regional export markets. Page C3.
